name: Baku State Circus
card_summary: The Baku State Circus is the city's main arena for circus performances. Enver Ismailov designed the building.

name: St. Nicholas Church
card_summary: The St. Nicholas Church was a Russian Orthodox Church completed in 1857. It was named after Saint Nicholas, and once stood in Baku.
narrative: The St. Nicholas Church was a Russian Orthodox Church. It was built in Baku between 1850 and 1857. The church was named after Saint Nicholas.

name: Cume Mescidi, Mashtaga
card_summary: Out in the Mashtaga settlement, the Cume Mescidi is a stone mosque from 1891. It's a quiet spot to see.

retrieval: Cume Mescidi, Mashtaga is a mosque located in the Mashtaga settlement, Sabunchi district, Baku. Constructed in 1891, it is built from stone.

name: Lökbatan Mud Volcano
card_summary: This is one of the world's most active mud volcanoes, located just southwest of Baku. It's known for its frequent eruptions and its surprising connection to local oil discoveries.
narrative: So, you've heard about the mud volcanoes, right? Lökbatan is a big one, actually among the top five most active in the world. It erupts pretty often, about every 3 to 10 years, and the last recorded one was just this past April. What's wild is that a well drilled here in 1933 proved a link between these volcanoes and oil fields. That discovery changed how they looked for oil around here, and that original well is still producing.
retrieval: Lökbatan Mud Volcano is a monument and Tentative World Heritage Site located 12-15km southwest of Baku, near the Caspian Sea coast. It is one of the world's five most active mud volcanoes, erupting approximately every 3-10 years, with 25 recorded eruptions since 1829, most recently on April 9, 2025. The volcano is notable for its role in proving the genetic link between mud volcanoes and oil fields in 1933, leading to significant oil and gas extraction.

name: Independence Museum of Azerbaijan
card_summary: The Independence Museum is a good place to get a sense of Azerbaijan's long path to becoming its own country. It traces the national independence movement from ancient times to the present day.
narrative: You know, the Independence Museum you'll visit today was established in 1991, though there was an earlier attempt at one back in 1919. It started with 7,000 exhibits, but now holds around 20,000 items. The main idea here is to show Azerbaijan's national independence movement, from ancient times right up to the present day. They've organized the story across six different halls, each covering a distinct period or theme. You'll find everything from old maps and art to currencies and books, all telling that story.
retrieval: The Independence Museum of Azerbaijan was established on January 9, 1991. It houses approximately 20,000 exhibits, including art, architecture, maps, pictures, books, and currencies. The museum's goal is to highlight Azerbaijan's national independence movement from ancient times to the present, with its exposition displayed across six halls.

name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
card_summary: This 15th-century palace complex, built by the Shirvanshahs, is a key part of Baku's UNESCO World Heritage site. It's worth a walk to see the various buildings, from the main palace to the mosque and mausoleum.
narrative: The Palace of the Shirvanshahs is a sprawling 15th-century complex, built by the Shirvanshahs themselves. You'll find the main palace, a mosque, and even burial vaults within its grounds. It's interesting that the construction dates are actually found on inscriptions on the tomb and minaret, not on the palace walls. This whole ensemble was once the inner stronghold of the Baku fortress, surrounded by its own wall and towers.
retrieval: The Palace of the Shirvanshahs is a 15th-century palace complex in Baku's Inner City, built by the Shirvanshahs. It comprises a main palace, Divanhane, burial-vaults, a shah's mosque with a minaret, and Seyid Yahya Bakuvi's mausoleum. Part of a UNESCO World Heritage ensemble, it has been a museum-preserve since 1964, with construction dates derived from inscriptions on the tomb and minaret.
